---
title: "Nets and dn0"
---

A net enters the models as two numbers: `dn0_use`, the probability that a mosquito is
killed when it contacts a treated net, and `itn_use`, the share of the population
sleeping under one. Which insecticide the net carries, and how resistant the local
mosquitoes have become, is compressed entirely into `dn0_use`.

`calculate_dn0` does that compression. It is the first call in almost every `estimint`
workflow.

## Net types

Four formulations are modelled. `net_types` returns their canonical names, alphabetically.

```{python}
from estimint import net_types, calculate_dn0

net_types()
```

Each has a short alias, accepted anywhere a net type is. The aliases double as the
keyword-argument names in the wider API.

| Alias | Canonical name | Formulation |
|---|---|---|
| `py_only` | `pyrethroid_only` | Pyrethroid alone |
| `py_pbo` | `pyrethroid_pbo` | Pyrethroid with PBO |
| `py_ppf` | `pyrethroid_ppf` | Pyrethroid with pyriproxyfen |
| `py_pyrrole` | `pyrethroid_pyrrole` | Pyrethroid with chlorfenapyr |

Both spellings are case-insensitive. The canonical names use underscores throughout, and a
hyphen raises `ValueError: unknown net type`.

## From a net mix to dn0

`calculate_dn0` takes a resistance level and the net mix as keyword arguments. Each keyword is
a net type, and each value is the share of the population using that net.

```{python}
net = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.70)
net
```

The return value is a `DN0Result`, a named tuple of exactly two fields. It unpacks and
attribute-accesses alike.

```{python}
net.dn0, net.itn_use
```

At 30% pyrethroid resistance, a pyrethroid-only net kills about 31% of the mosquitoes that
contact it. Coverage is 70%.

A mix passes more than one net type. Here 40% of the population has pyrethroid-only nets and
30% has PBO nets. The remaining 30% has no net at all.

```{python}
mix = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.40, py_pbo=0.30)
mix
```

## The weighted average and the sum

The two fields are constructed differently. Conflating them is the most common error in the
package.

`dn0` is the **usage-weighted average** of the per-net-type `dn0` values across the mix. That
makes it a property of the nets that exist rather than of how many people happen to have them.
The weights are normalised. Reconstruct it by hand.

```{python}
only = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=1.0).dn0
pbo = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_pbo=1.0).dn0

by_hand = (0.40 * only + 0.30 * pbo) / (0.40 + 0.30)
round(by_hand, 5), round(mix.dn0, 5)
```

`itn_use` is the **sum** of the shares, 0.40 + 0.30 = 0.70. It is the total ITN coverage of the
population, and it is already complete.

::: {.callout-warning}
## A note on `itn_use`

`DN0Result.itn_use` is the finished coverage figure, not a weight awaiting a coverage term.
Multiplying it by a usage fraction a second time understates the coverage, and the error is
silent.

```{python}
net = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.70)

net.itn_use, round(net.itn_use * 0.70, 3)  # the second value is the mistake
```

The model then reads a district with 49% net coverage rather than 70%, and understates
the EIR. The size of that error is measured in
[Estimating EIR from prevalence](estimating-eir.qmd).
:::

## Resistance and dn0

Holding usage at 1.0 isolates each formulation's resistance response.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

levels = [0.0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0]

table = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        f"{r:.2f}": [calculate_dn0(r, **{nt: 1.0}).dn0 for nt in net_types()]
        for r in levels
    },
    index=net_types(),
).round(4)
table.index.name = "net type"
table
```

Read across a row for the decay of one formulation, and down a column to compare
formulations at a fixed resistance.

The `dn0` of a pyrethroid-only net falls to zero at full resistance. The other three retain
some lethality across the whole range.

Pyrrole nets are the most lethal and the flattest. They lose only about a tenth of their `dn0`
between resistance 0.0 and 0.75, where a pyrethroid-only net loses nearly a third.

PPF nets have a low `dn0` throughout the table. Their effect on the next generation is not
represented in `dn0` at all, and appears only in the scenario pipeline.

The resistance-to-`dn0` curves come from the same published source that
`malariasimulation` uses.

## Caveats

`dn0` summarises the kill on contact and nothing else. It captures neither repellence nor the
loss of a net to wear and disuse over a campaign. The resistance level you supply should be the
local pyrethroid resistance at the decision point, and a single net mix is assumed to hold
across the population.
